writeup.headline: Alnylam rates Hold: strong balance sheet and quality offset by weak share-price trend and high absolute valuation.
writeup.thesis: Alnylam scores 48, a Hold that sits only 4 points above the Sell band. The balance sheet is the standout at 100, with net cash and cash at 3.54 times debt, and quality scores 65 on an 81.8% gross margin, 13.5% operating margin and a diluted share count up 0.5% year on year. Growth scores 61: TTM revenue growth of 65.2% is strong, but latest-quarter revenue growth of 16.7% year on year shows growth slowed by 50.1 pp from the previous quarter. Valuation scores 23 because absolute multiples are high (8.4x sales, 66.9x FCF, 56.9x EV/EBIT, FCF yield 3.5 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield), even though it is cheap against its own history (P/FCF and EV/EBIT not comparable), with P/S cheaper than at 60 of the last 61 month-ends. The trend score of 6 drags hardest, with the price 51.7% below its 52-week high and shares 31.9 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days.
key_risks: Sharp growth deceleration: growth slowed by 50.1 pp from the previous quarter
High absolute valuation, with FCF yield 3.5 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield
Persistent price weakness: shares down 46.9% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago
Competitive pressure on Amvuttra from Pfizer's Vyndamax and BridgeBio's Attruby, plus heavy reliance on that one product
Brokers cutting price targets, including a steep cut from UBS
what_would_change: A 4-point drop in the score would move the rating to Sell, for example from further price weakness or another slowdown in growth
Reaching Buy needs 17 more points, most plausibly from a recovery in the trend score (now 6) alongside steady growth
Margin expansion that lifts FCF and lowers P/FCF and EV/EBIT would improve the valuation score of 23
A guidance raise or analyst upgrades would lift the news risk score from 51
